solution-list.description: Solution 1 - Brute Force Approach: Try every possible subarray and compute its sum. Time Complexity: O(n^2). Java file: LongestSubarrayBruteForce.java

Solution 2 - HashMap Version: Keep track of the running prefix sum in a HashMap and store the first occurrence of each prefix sum. If (prefixSum - k) exists, we found a valid subarray. Time Complexity: O(n). Java file: LongestSubarrayHashMap.java

hints: Think about prefix sums.

Store the first occurrence of each prefix sum.

description: Given the root of a BST and two node values p and q, find their Lowest Common Ancestor. The LCA is the deepest node that has both p and q as descendants, where a node counts as a descendant of itself.
title: Binary Search Tree: Lowest Common Ancestor

question-content.section-text: Exploit BST ordering to find where the two nodes diverge.
section-content: The LCA is the deepest shared ancestor of two nodes.
BST ordering helps narrow the search direction.
If both values are less than root go left, if both greater go right.
